inputs: docs/specs/fleetd/amendments.md (Systems review round, fix round 2 and closing fix, A23 to A37)

assumptions.text: The 6 contexts are modules inside horch-core in 1 deployable unit and 1 team (understand N6). The boundaries are model boundaries, not process boundaries.
The verifier stays a module of task-execution because it reads and writes the same task states and the reap rule (04 S7) needs 1 transaction. Decision D1, option A (orchestrator, D15).

The question aggregate (worker-question-asked to question-escalated) belongs to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator answers it against the idea's assumptions. Decision D2, option A (orchestrator, D15).

Worker profiles and adapters are their own context because of their rate of change and their credential rules, although the storm holds only 3 of their events (discover H14, N10). Decision D3, option A (orchestrator, D15).
Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15).
The ledger is infrastructure that fleet-runtime owns as the single writer. Each context owns the state transitions of its own aggregates; it is not a shared kernel.

Operator attention (cap-operator-attention) maps to ideas. There is 1 needs-you list (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/), and ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15): approvals, interview questions, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. task-execution emits task-escalated, and ideas puts it on the list.
Triage and resolver tasks are opened by integration but run as normal tasks in task-execution; integration asks task-execution for them.
Each preservation row has 1 owning context, as listed in N3. The row texts come from the Preservation analysis of design.md.

The platform layer is not a bounded context and has no subdomain. It is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform (design A19, understand N13), and each context calls it directly. fleet-runtime uses it like every other context.

worker-profiles owns start-agent-process and agent-process-started: it starts the fleet-run wrapper of an attempt, or the herdr pane of a sub-orchestrator, from the launch environment of the profile (discover N10). This keeps the environment scrub with 1 owner (decision D3).

notes_for_downstream.text: Sharpens understand N6: all 6 contexts are modules inside horch-core in 1 deployable; worktree-custody (ISH unsure) and fleet-runtime (ISH merge) are never deployables of their own.

Sharpens understand N16: worker-profiles owns the environment scrub. It builds the env of every launch (attempt, sub-orchestrator pane, probe, updater), so task-execution and ideas launch only through it.

Sharpens discover N8. Preservation row owners: worktree-custody 04 W6, W8, W9; integration 04 F5, F7, F9, F11, L5, L9; task-execution 04 S7, S8, L6, L8 and 06 S13; worker-profiles 05 E-10, 06 S1, S3 to S10, S15; fleet-runtime 04 S10, 04 M5, 06 S2, S11, S12.

'Check' means the task acceptance command in task-execution and horch fleetd check (the heartbeat check) in fleet-runtime. 'Lease' means the attempt lease in task-execution and the worktree lease in worktree-custody.

Sharpens understand N5: fleet-runtime owns the single ledger writer and the command channel. Every other context changes the ledger only through it; each context still owns the legal transitions of its own aggregates. From Phase 5 only (A36): in Phases 1 to 4 the horch commands also write, through the same transition().

The task branch and the worktree are 2 aggregates in 2 contexts with 1 lifecycle link: a worktree goes to landing when its task branch is verified and to landed when the branch is landed. The link crosses R6 and R8.

Sharpens understand N13: the platform layer (crates/horch-platform, design A19) is not a bounded context, has no subdomain, and fleet-runtime does not own it. Each of the 6 contexts calls it directly. R12 and R13 carry only the ledger writer, the command channel and the herdr adapter.

worker-profiles owns start-agent-process and agent-process-started (discover N10, A11). attempt-launched in task-execution and start-sub-orchestrator in ideas both start their process through it, so the environment scrub has 1 owner.
There is 1 needs-you list (design OR-3), and ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15). task-execution emits task-escalated, and ideas puts the task on the list beside approvals and escalated questions.

The orchestrator (D15) took option A of D1 to D4: the verifier is a module of task-execution, worker questions belong to ideas, worker-profiles and worktree-custody are contexts of their own. The 6 contexts and 13 links stay. Round 3 adds R14 to R16 (fleet-runtime to integration, worktree-custody and worker-profiles: the ledger writer and the job runner). 6 contexts and 16 links.

Long work is a job (A23, A32, A33). fleet-runtime owns the job runner: the jobs table, the run number, the bound on abandoned runs, observe-jobs and horch job requeue. Each context owns its job kinds and acts on their results: task-execution task_check; integration bundle_build, fast_gate, full_gate, trial_merge, rebase, fetch, push; worktree-custody worktree_add, worktree_remove, worktree_list, rescue; worker-profiles docs_sync, conformance. R14 to R16 carry it.

fleet-runtime owns the reconcile pass in 3 parts (facts, 1 transaction, effects), each effect row in an intended state first, the work and time budgets with pass_cursors, the fleet clock, the fleetd lock and generation number, and the requests table with its request classes and the operator token check (A24, A25, A32, A35). worker-profiles owns the 1 launcher (SR-7) and the sandbox deny rules of each worker profile (SR-8, A37).

integration owns the bundle state machine (bundles, bundle_members), the feature state machine (open, ready, merged, abandoned), remote_tips, push_state and pr_state, and repair_attempts of a task branch (A27, A28, A34). integration also owns move-ideas-to-new-feature for a merge with ideas in flight, because it is a rule of the feature; ideas takes the new feature of each idea from the event (R9). worktree-custody owns the 2 rescue ref classes and horch rescue drop.

task-execution owns the exit to cancelled from each task state that is not terminal (cancel-task, A34). The order: stop the process group of a live attempt, cancel the task, then integration writes a rescue ref and abandons the task branch (R6). The cancel of a judged task also cancels its judge task.

The design (A31, D15) now states the module owners with the same names as this step: the wrapper and the launcher belong to worker-profiles, plan validation and the needs-you list belong to ideas, git has 2 callers (worktree-custody, integration), task-execution and integration are a partnership, docs sync is a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules, and an arch_scan rule enforces the module boundaries.

decisions.question: Is the verifier a context of its own, or a module of task-execution?

options.summary: Module of task-execution: verification is an aggregate beside task and attempt.
pros: 1 transaction for attempt end, verdict and task state
The skill tie-break says merge when the boundary is unsure
cons: The judge rank language (CRITICAL, HIGH) sits beside lease language

options.summary: Context of its own (verification) that task-execution calls after attempt-exited.
pros: Keeps judge and review rules apart from dispatch
cons: Every done needs a cross-context call and an event back
risks: The reap and requeue rule 04 S7 spans 2 contexts

options.summary: Merge verification into integration, since both run gates.
cons: Mixes task done with branch landed, which the design keeps apart (understand N4)
risks: The word done changes meaning inside 1 model

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommend A. Verification shares the task states and the transaction of task-execution. Strongest argument against: the design lists the Verifier as its own component with its own rules for each task kind, so its rules may change apart from dispatch.
would_flip_if: The judge and review rules change on a different schedule from dispatch

decisions.question: Which context owns worker questions: ideas or task-execution?

pros: The sub-orchestrator answers against the idea's assumptions
revise-requested goes to the operator approval flow of the idea
cons: The worker, an actor of task-execution, asks it
risks: The attempt pause and resume crosses 2 contexts

pros: The attempt waits on it, so pause and resume stay inside 1 context
cons: Answers create assumptions that belong to the idea

options.summary: A context of its own (operator attention) for questions, approvals and escalations.
cons: A seventh context above the 2 to 6 band at 1 deployable
risks: A thin context with no own language

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommend A. The answer is an assumption of the idea. Strongest argument against: the attempt pause and resume then depends on another context. Source: design, the owner of a worker question is the sub-orchestrator of its feature (RR-12).
would_flip_if: Answers never change the idea's assumptions

decisions.question: Are worker profiles and adapters a context of their own, or a part of task-execution?

pros: Rate of change of the CLIs
1 owner for the credential and environment rules
risks: A thin context until docs sync is stormed

cons: CLI churn changes the dispatch model
risks: The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rule has no clear owner

options.summary: Part of fleet-runtime, as a platform concern.
cons: Profiles are domain choices, not OS facilities
risks: fleet-runtime mixes OS and CLI churn

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommend A. The CLI adapters change weekly and carry the absolute credential rule. Strongest argument against: the storm shows only 2 events, and the skill tie-break says merge when unsure. Reason of the orchestrator: the environment scrub has 1 owner.
would_flip_if: The docs sync storm shows no own language

decisions.question: Is worktree custody a context of its own, or a part of integration?

pros: Own meaning of lease and landed
Only fleetd creates or removes worktrees, from 1 place

cons: A worktree exists from task-leased, long before landing
risks: Landing changes can break the no-loss rules

options.summary: Part of task-execution, beside the attempt.
pros: The worktree is leased with the task
cons: The worktree survives attempts and outlives the task until landed
risks: Rescue logic mixes with the stall ladder

decisions.rationale: Decided by the orchestrator (D15). The operator can reverse it. Recommend A. The worktree has its own lifecycle and its own no-loss rows. Strongest argument against: integration also writes git, so 2 contexts adapt 1 external system.
would_flip_if: The worktree lifecycle is folded into the task branch lifecycle
No-loss rules move into git hooks

subdomains.name: Ideas
subdomains.description: Takes a rough idea from capture to a committed plan, answers worker questions, and closes the idea when its feature is merged. The idea dispatcher (code) moves each idea; the sub-orchestrator does the judgment work.
subdomains.rationale: The clarifying and planning phases end at the pivotal events assumptions-approved and plan-committed. The operator and the sub-orchestrator drive almost every command here, and nowhere else (discover N7).

subdomains.name: Task execution
subdomains.description: Dispatches each task of a committed plan to a worker, supervises each attempt with an earned lease and the stall ladder, paces dispatch to each usage pool, and decides done from facts on disk.
subdomains.rationale: The executing phase runs from plan-committed to the pivotal event task-done. Workers, the agent CLI process and the clock act here; the operator acts only on an escalated task.

subdomains.name: Worktree custody
subdomains.description: Records each worktree before it exists, reconciles the ledger rows, the directories and git, and saves the work of each worktree on a verified rescue ref before any removal.
subdomains.rationale: The worktree lifecycle (reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed) crosses the executing and landing phases. Its no-loss rules change rarely and must not change with the landing or dispatch rules.

subdomains.name: Landing and integration
subdomains.description: Lands verified task branches on their feature branch in gated bundles, finds conflicts between features by trial merges, rebases and gates each feature branch, and opens its pull request to the primary branch.
subdomains.rationale: The landing and integrating phases run from task-done through idea-tasks-landed to feature-merged. Only fleetd code acts here, until the operator merges the pull request (discover N7).

subdomains.name: Worker profiles and adapters
subdomains.description: Turns 1 worker profile into the exact flags, environment and files for each agent CLI, keeps logins and environment scrubs, mirrors CLI docs and runs adapter conformance tests.
subdomains.rationale: Agent CLIs change every week, much faster than the fleet rules. The credential rules (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub, logins, sandbox) need 1 owner.

subdomains.name: Fleet runtime
subdomains.description: Keeps fleetd alive under the OS service manager, restarts it on a hang or a new binary, owns the command channel, the file protocol permissions and the single ledger writer, and adapts herdr. It runs each job outside the reconcile pass and keeps the fleet clock (A23, A25).
subdomains.rationale: The friend who installs horch and the OS service manager act here, and no domain phase does. Its OS concerns (service install, restart, hang detection) change with the OS, not with the fleet rules, and reach the OS through the platform layer, which is not a context (understand N13, A10).

bounded_contexts.name: Ideas

terms.meaning_here: 1 line in assumptions.md, [confirmed] or [assumed], that the operator approves or revises; also a reversible assumption that the sub-orchestrator records to answer a worker question (understand N11).
A worker question to the sub-orchestrator of its feature. It ends as an answer, an own assumption, a revise request, or an escalation to the operator.
Not a role in fleetd. The word survives only in the preserved mail contract tag [orchestrator re #<id>] (discover N3).
The 1 place for everything that waits for the operator (design OR-3, /fleet/needs-you/): approvals, escalated worker questions and escalated tasks. ideas owns it (orchestrator, D15).

bounded_contexts.rationale: Cut at the pivotal events assumptions-approved and plan-committed (pivotal-event) and by the actor change: operator and sub-orchestrator own clarifying and planning (discover N7). The idea, plan and question aggregates live here because the sub-orchestrator answers worker questions against the idea's assumptions (own-assumption-recorded, revise-requested). Closest alternative: put question in task-execution, where the worker asks it (decision D2). The idea dispatcher is code, not an actor; no 'orchestrator' actor exists (understand N3). From A28 it also plans the ideas of 1 feature in order, and keeps the needs-you list with its life cycle (open, resolved, superseded).

bounded_contexts.name: Task execution

terms.meaning_here: The time-limited hold of 1 attempt on its task. It renews only on earned activity and pauses during sleep and waiting_quota (discover N1).
A task state: every dependency is done and the task waits for dispatch (discover N6).
A task state that only the verifier sets, from facts on disk. It does not mean landed or merged (understand N4).
The acceptance command of a task. The verifier runs it in the worktree, in the sandbox profile of the worker.
A code kind of a task (with quality, refactor and security). It is not the feature of the integration context (discover N2).

bounded_contexts.rationale: Cut between plan-committed and task-done (pivotal-event). Task, attempt and verification are 3 aggregate candidates with 1 shared language (task, attempt, lease, done) and 1 transaction rule: a reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 transaction (04 S7). The verifier is a separate component in the design, but it reads and writes the same task states, so it stays a module here (decision D1). The context adapts the agent CLI process (attempt-exited, through the fleet-run wrapper) and the provider pools (usage-limit-reported, quota-window-reset); both adapters are internal. From A26 and A34 it owns the task state table of 12 states with 1 owner and 1 exit each, the exit to cancelled from each state that is not terminal, the outcomes that burn no attempt (asked, quota, critical_open) and the judge pair with fix_rounds.

bounded_contexts.name: Worktree custody

terms.meaning_here: The worktree lease: the ledger row written in the same transaction that leases the task, before the directory exists. It holds the worktree for 1 task until its work is landed or rescued.
A worktree state: nothing in the worktree is unique any more, so fleetd may remove it (discover N6).
A worktree on disk with no live owner attempt, or with no ledger row.

bounded_contexts.rationale: The worktree outlives attempts (understand N1) and its 'lease' and 'landed' mean different things from the attempt lease and the task branch state (language-boundary). Only this context may create or remove a worktree, and it owns the no-loss rows 04 W6, W8 and W9 (data-ownership, discover N8). Closest alternative: merge it into integration, which also changes git state (decision D4). It adapts git for worktree add, list and rescue refs; integration adapts git for branches. From A27 and A32 it also owns the worktree_add, worktree_remove, worktree_list and rescue job kinds, the 2 classes of rescue ref (unique, superseded) and horch rescue drop.

bounded_contexts.name: Landing and integration

terms.meaning_here: 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request to the primary branch, holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas (understand N2). The feature aggregate owns feature-opened to feature-merged (discover N2).
A task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle. A feature is ready when its full gate passed and its pull request can open (discover N6).
A task branch state: the branch is fast-forwarded onto its feature branch after the fast gate passed (understand N4).
A feature fact read from git by content: the feature branch is in the primary branch (understand N4).
A bundles row: 1 candidate of ready task branches of 1 feature on 1 base tip, with the states building, gating, passed, landed, failed and dropped. A bisect part is a child bundle (A27, A34).

bounded_contexts.rationale: Cut at task-done and idea-tasks-landed (pivotal-event): after task-done the words change to branch, bundle, gate and merge, and only fleetd code acts (actor). The task-branch and feature aggregates and the land lock live here, with the no-loss rows 04 F5, F7, F9, F11, L5 and L9 (data-ownership). It adapts git (primary-branch-moved) and GitHub (pull-request-merged). From A27, A28 and A34 it also owns the bundle state machine, the compare-and-set of each ref move, the repair attempts of a task branch, the feature state machine (open, ready, merged, abandoned), the push and fetch jobs with push_state, pr_state and remote_tips, and horch feature abandon and horch branch abandon.

bounded_contexts.name: Worker profiles and adapters

terms.meaning_here: A named worker profile: the CLI, model, effort, sandbox and permission rules that 1 attempt runs with.
A profile whose adapter passed its last conformance test. Dispatch does not choose an unhealthy profile.

bounded_contexts.rationale: Rate-of-change: CLI versions and flags change far more often than the task rules. Language: profile, adapter, persona and conformance appear nowhere else. Regulatory: it owns the environment scrub and login rules (05 E-10, 06 S1, S3 to S10, S15), so the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rule has exactly 1 owner (understand N16). The storm holds only 3 of its events (discover H14, plus agent-process-started of discover N10), so decision D3 records the merge alternative. It starts each agent process from the launch environment of its profile (start-agent-process), so no other context builds a launch. From A29, A35 and A37 it also owns the 1 launcher that starts each process with the environment rule of the profile, profile health (unhealthy and healthy again), the sandbox deny rules of each worker (the operator token, the command channel, the request folder), and the refusal of a profile on an OS where its sandbox is not supported (06 S9).

bounded_contexts.name: Fleet runtime

terms.meaning_here: horch fleetd check: the heartbeat check that restarts fleetd when its last full pass is older than 30 s of awake time. It is not a task check.

A jobs row and its process: work that can take more than 1 s and runs outside the reconcile pass. fleet-runtime runs and observes each job; the context that queues a job kind acts on its result (A23, A33).
The count of seconds in the fleetd row that each pass advances. Every operational deadline of every context is on it (A25).

bounded_contexts.rationale: External-system: it wraps the OS service managers and herdr, which hold no state that fleetd depends on (understand N14: do not build, only wrap). It does not own the platform layer: the platform layer is the leaf crate crates/horch-platform that each context calls, not a context (design A19, understand N13, A10). fleet-runtime calls it for the service manager and hang detection. It owns the single ledger writer and the command channel (understand N5) as infrastructure for every other context, and the rows 04 S10, 04 M5, 06 S2, S11 and S12. ISH verdict merge: it is a module, never a product of its own. From the systems review (A23 to A37) it also owns the reconcile pass in 3 parts with its work and time budgets and pass_cursors, the fleet clock, the fleetd lock and generation number, the job runner (the jobs table, observe-jobs, horch job requeue), and the requests table with the request classes and the operator token check of the command channel.

relationships.description: ideas -> integration, published-language: assumptions-written and direct-idea-accepted (ideaId, featureId) trigger open-feature. Upstream is ideas because the idea events are its to change. Integration consumes them as-is and needs no change in ideas, so not customer-supplier. Async through the reconcile pass.

ideas -> task-execution, customer-supplier: plan-committed and task-replanned trigger promote-task; plan-refused triggers escalate-task; question-answered and own-assumption-recorded trigger launch-attempt. The committed plan.yaml is the contract that every task comes from, and plan validation exists to serve task-execution (checks, owner paths, paired judges), so task-execution's needs shape ideas' plan schema. Async. From A34: idea-cancelled triggers cancel-task for each task of the idea that is not terminal.

task-execution -> ideas, published-language: replan-requested (taskId, attempts) triggers replan-task by the sub-orchestrator after the last attempt. ideas consumes the event as-is. Separate from R2 because the direction of influence is reversed for this fact. Async.

task-execution -> worktree-custody, customer-supplier: task-leased triggers create-worktree; the worktree lease row is written in the same transaction as the task lease. worktree-custody serves the dispatch need (1 worktree per task before launch). The pair also carries the attempt end: active to created or orphaned. Sync inside the fleetd pass.

worktree-custody -> task-execution, published-language: worktree-created triggers launch-attempt; rescue-failed triggers escalate-task. task-execution reacts to worktree facts as-is. Async through the reconcile pass.

task-execution -> integration, partnership (orchestrator, D15): task-done triggers mark-branch-ready; task-escalated lets the operator run abandon-task-branch. Integration asks task-execution to run triage and resolver tasks (open-triage-task, open-resolver-task create normal tasks). R6 and R7 change together: the 2 contexts plan their changes together. Async. From A34: task-cancelled triggers abandon-task-branch after a rescue ref; attempt-failed of a resolver or fix attempt at max_attempts triggers escalate-task-branch.

integration -> task-execution, partnership (orchestrator, D15): task-branch-conflicted triggers launch-attempt on the same task. R6 and R7 change together: the 2 contexts plan their changes together. Async. From A27: task-branch-gate-failed starts a fix attempt of the task; task-branch-repair-escalated lets the operator run requeue-task.

integration -> worktree-custody, published-language: task-branch-landed triggers remove-worktree; the worktree moves to landing and landed with its task branch (N6). worktree-custody still refuses a removal that would lose work (04 W6). Async.

integration -> ideas, published-language: task-branch-landed triggers roll-up-idea, and feature-merged triggers close-idea. ideas consumes branch facts as-is and never reads git. Async. From A28: ideas-moved-to-new-feature (a merge with ideas in flight, owned by integration with the feature) gives each such idea its new feature, and feature-abandoned triggers cancel-idea.

worker-profiles -> task-execution, customer-supplier: launch-attempt resolves a profile to exact CLI flags, environment and files, with the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY scrub (N2); profile-marked-unhealthy removes a profile from dispatch and fallback. task-execution needs profiles that fit its dispatch and fallback rules and can negotiate them. attempt-launched triggers start-agent-process (policy start-process-on-launch), and worker-profiles starts the fleet-run wrapper and emits agent-process-started (A11). Sync at launch.

worker-profiles -> ideas, customer-supplier: start-sub-orchestrator launches a sub-orchestrator pane with a profile and the same environment scrub. The pane starts through start-agent-process too. Sync at launch. From the design (Docs sync and adapter conformance): adapter-conformance-failed triggers add-idea, so a drift becomes an idea.

fleet-runtime -> task-execution, open-host-service: fleet-runtime gives the single ledger writer (N5) through 1 interface. The platform layer is not part of this link: task-execution calls the leaf crate crates/horch-platform directly for process facts, process-group stop, sandbox, sleep and wake (A10). The same interface serves every context, so open-host-service, not customer-supplier. Sync calls. From A23: fleet-runtime also runs each job that task-execution queues (task_check) through the same interface.

fleet-runtime -> ideas, open-host-service: the command channel carries horch idea commands to fleetd, and the herdr adapter hosts and supervises sub-orchestrator panes. Same interface as R12. Sync calls.

fleet-runtime -> integration, open-host-service: fleet-runtime gives the single ledger writer and the job runner (A23, A33). integration queues the jobs bundle_build, fast_gate, full_gate, trial_merge, rebase, fetch and push and acts on their results. Async: a pass never waits for a job.

fleet-runtime -> worktree-custody, open-host-service: the single ledger writer and the job runner (A23, A32). worktree-custody queues the jobs worktree_add, worktree_remove, worktree_list and rescue and acts on their results. Async.

fleet-runtime -> worker-profiles, open-host-service: the single ledger writer and the job runner (A33). fleetd queues the docs_sync and conformance jobs, and worker-profiles acts on their results. Async.

plain_words.what: This step cut fleetd into 6 parts, each with its own words and its own data: ideas, task execution, worktree custody, landing and integration, worker profiles, and the fleet runtime.
plain_words.decided: 6 parts, all modules inside the 1 horch binary, joined by 13 named links. Each of the 83 events and 65 commands has exactly 1 owner. The platform layer is a shared library that every part calls, not a part.
plain_words.assumed: The verifier lives inside task execution, and worker questions live inside ideas. The orchestrator chose both (D1, D2), and the operator can reverse them.
plain_words.riskiest: If worker profiles is not its own part, the rule that strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from every launch has no single owner, and 1 missed launch path bills the API key.

deprecated.reason: Answered (orchestrator, D15): decision D4, option A. Worktree custody is its own context. Recorded in D4 and A5.
Answered (orchestrator, D15): there is 1 needs-you list, and ideas owns it. An escalated task goes on that list. Recorded in A7, the ideas term Needs-you list and N9.

Answered (orchestrator, D15): worker-profiles marks a profile unhealthy and healthy again, because it owns the profiles and the conformance results. The docs sync subcommand reports a drift to ideas as a --direct idea, so ideas creates the task.
